title: CareLine Service Plans — One Plan per Customer
content:
**Enrollment desk guidance, CareLine Service Plans.**

> A plan covers one service address, and each customer profile has one service address, so a customer holds one service account or plan at a time. A new plan can be opened only when the customer holds no plan that is active or past due; to move to another plan, the holder cancels the current one first.

The limit is 1 plan per customer: one On-Call Service Account or one CareLine plan, never two at once.

### Basis

- **Whose plans count.** Every plan on record for the same customer counts, whatever its tier — an On-Call Service Account counts as much as a CareLine plan.
- **What decides it.** The plan records and their statuses as the system shows them before the new plan is opened, not the customer's account of what they hold.
- **Which statuses stand in the way.** Active and past due. A plan that is cancelled or expired does not.
- **What a new plan is.** A new plan is a separate record with its own plan number; it does not reopen or reuse a plan already on record.

### Status check, condition by condition

| The customer's plans on record | May a new plan be opened under this rule? |
|---|---|
| One plan, active | No |
| One plan, past due | No |
| One plan, cancelled | This rule does not stand in the way |
| One plan, expired | This rule does not stand in the way |
| One cancelled and one expired plan | This rule does not stand in the way |
| No plan at all | This rule does not stand in the way |

### Hypothetical cases

1. A customer's CareLine Basic Plan is active and the customer asks for the CareLine Premier Plan. Under this rule a new plan cannot be opened while the Basic plan is active; to move to another plan, the holder cancels the current one first.
2. A customer's CareLine Plus Plan is past due because its renewal fee is unpaid. A past-due plan stands in the way of a new plan just as an active one does.
3. A customer's On-Call Service Account expired last year. An expired account does not stand in the way of a new plan.
